widgets_values:
Exercise: the two-stage seam fix, composed from the two packaged
blueprints - the realistic panorama case where aligned views disagree in
BOTH exposure and texture.

Stage 1 - 'CV Exposure Match': B' is B under-exposed x0.7 (+10), matched
back to A per BGR channel with whole-image statistics (the mask input is
left unconnected = measure everywhere; in a real mosaic you would scope
it to the true overlap).

Stage 2 - blend along the half/hard boundary three ways:
  * raw hard cut: brightness STEP at the seam plus a texture switch
  * matched hard cut: the step is gone - but Starry Night's swirls still
    switch to waves along a knife-edge line, which reads as an artifact
  * matched MULTI-BAND: coarse structure of the transition spreads across
    a wide band while fine detail switches sharply - no step, no ghost,
    no visible seam at all

Order matters: blending CANNOT fix a brightness step (multi-band would
smoothly cross BETWEEN different exposures, i.e. smear the step), and
matching alone cannot hide a texture switch. The pipeline is
align -> match exposure -> blend.

In a real stitch: fit the homography first ('Feature Match + RANSAC
Homography'), warp into the mosaic frame, then run these two stages with
the overlap region as the statistics mask.

nodes.title: White RIGHT half = take view B' there
[CV Exposure Match (Masked Per-Channel)] Match B' -> A (stats over whole frames)
Raw hard cut (exposure step at the seam)
Matched hard cut (step gone, textures still switch)
[CV Multi-Band Blend (Laplacian pyramid)] Multi-band blend of A + matched B'
